name: Tubular Bells
notes:
tubularBellsSeed: orchestral tubular bells — REBUILT 2026-08-22 from scratch
per the listener's own verdict: "simple clean tone vs resonant wavy metallic
ring that prolongs" ("scrape this and try again from scratch"). The old
2-op FM voice (single inharmonic ratio 1.41, one shared decay) measured only
TWO partials (1.00, 3.00x f0) against the reference's SEVEN non-consecutive
ones, and its overall post-peak decay rate (-6.5 dB/s) was ~1.5x faster than
the reference's (-4.3 dB/s) even though both clips clamp at the same 2.97s
clip-length ceiling (see ringT60Axis's decay-rate escalation).

New architecture: ADDITIVE gens placed directly at the reference's own
measured partial ratios (tubular-bells-vcsl: 0.62, 1.01, 1.47, 1.71, 2.01,
2.61, 3.26x f0 -- a genuine inharmonic, non-consecutive struck-tube series,
not a mistuned harmonic stack), each with its OWN per-gen decay rate (higher
partials fade faster, matching real bell/bar physics -- same technique as
xylophoneSeed/bassoonSeed's per-partial gen_env_fast_rate). amp_decay and
amp_release are both pinned at 4.0 -- the ParamDef schema's declared max
for both (modular_recipe.go) -- so those per-gen rates (not the master
envelope) govern the audible ring length, closing the "prolongs" gap. Two
partials are placed half a percent apart (1.01 and 1.015x f0) so they beat
against each other at a few Hz -- the "waving" the listener described -- and
a slow lfo_target:0 amplitude wobble reinforces the same effect (also moves
the "sustain modulation" bonus axis). gen_env_fast_mix defaults to 1 with
fast_rate>0 ⇒ genuine DECAY (not a sustained bed) per each partial's own rate.

RESULT (headline axis): ring T60 moved MISMATCH-adjacent drift (-6.5 dB/s,
worse than the OLD FM voice was) -> ok (-5.0 dB/s vs ref -4.3 dB/s) after
three iterations: (1) amp_release was originally left short (0.6-1.2s) and
was silently truncating the ring during the reference's own note-off
window -- raised toward the schema max so the per-gen decay rates, not the
release stage, govern the tail; (2) the initial per-gen fast_rate values
(guessed from bell physics, ~0.12-1.2) still decayed ~1.5x too fast in
aggregate -- scaled ALL of them down ~4x to land the measured overall
decay rate on the reference's; (3) an intermediate pass set amp_decay/
amp_release to 16.0/20.0, which measured fine via `refs diagnose` (that
tool renders through the same clamped recipe path real gameplay uses --
see below) but silently diverged from the Sampler-preview's no-edit fast
path, which applies the raw seed with NO clamp -- caught by
TestModularNoEditFastPathMatchesRecipe. Pinned both at 4.0 (the schema's
actual ceiling for amp_decay/amp_release, modular_recipe.go) so the two
paths render identically; this changes nothing about the ACTUAL rendered
audio measured above, since BuildBuiltinRecipeDocs (synth_recipe.go)
already clamped the seed to [Min,Max] when building this recipe's
ParamDef.Default -- 16.0/20.0 were already being played back as 4.0/4.0
everywhere except the no-edit fast path.

KNOWN CAVEAT (bonus axes, not this instrument's headline): refs diagnose's
own F0 detector locks onto ~1/6.5x the true fundamental for this recipe
specifically at the reference's high render pitch (~932Hz) -- confirmed via
cmd/synth-analyze (pitch=0 detects correctly at 221Hz; pitch=+25, the
reference's own transposition, detects 144Hz instead of ~932Hz) -- a
pre-existing tool limitation with inharmonic, weak-low-partial material at
high absolute pitch (same family of issue flagged for harp/kalimba/rimshot
in AGENTS.synth.instruments.md), not a synthesis defect: the measured
partial RATIOS scale in perfect lockstep with the intended design ratios,
just against the wrong anchor. This inflates "partial series deviation"
into MISMATCH even though the actual spectral structure is the intended
non-consecutive one. "sustain modulation" also overshot into MISMATCH
(too much wobble, having previously been "ok" pre-rebuild) from the
gen2/gen3 beat pair + LFO combination; lfo_depth was already pulled back
0.15->0.04 to reduce the overshoot without removing the beating character.

lfo.notes:
lfo_enabled: slow amplitude wobble -- reinforces the "waves in time" character
alongside the gen2/gen3 beat pair (belt-and-suspenders on the same axis).

layers.notes: gen1_source: hum (sub-partial, slowest decay -- bell hum tones linger longest)
gen2_source: prime/strike partial (~1x f0) -- the dominant perceived pitch

gen3_source: close beating partner (~0.5% away from gen2) -- slow amplitude "wave"
from real partial-to-partial beating, not just an LFO trick.
